To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zinc and cadmium are potent inhibitors of papain.
the enzyme papain is inactivated in presence of two metal ions zinc and cadmium in a concentration dependent fashion.
zinc and cadmium ions are potent inhibitors for papain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of two metal ions namely zinc(II) and cadmium(II) on the structure and catalytic function of papain.
the study of the influence of zinc and cadmium ions on the structural and functional aspects of papain.
understanding the influence of metal ions on papain activity and its mechanism of inhibition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal ions bind to the active site of papain, thereby decreasing the activity of the enzyme.
papain in presence both of zinc and cadmium metal ions is partially inactivated by the former and completely inactivated by the latter.
papain is a metal ion sensitive enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metal ions are not only acting as potent inhibitor of papain but also they are causing structural changes in papain molecule.
papain in presence either of Zn2+ or Cd2+ is inactivated by a mechanism involving a conformational change.
papain in presence or absence of metal ions has been investigated in detail by using different techniques and the mechanism for the inactivation of the enzyme by these metal ions has been proposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the papain molecule is more susceptible to metal ions than to the substrates.
the metal ions bind to the papain molecule in a non-specific manner and cause partial and complete inactivations of the enzyme at lower and higher concentrations respectively.
papain is not a metalloenzyme.
